reasoning: Paf1 encodes a core subunit of the PAF1 transcription‑elongation complex, which facilitates RNAP II processivity and deposition of activating histone marks (H3K4me3, H3K36me3).  Although there is no reported direct binding of PAF1 to the Nek10 promoter, loss of this co‑activator typically leads to reduced transcription of genes that depend on efficient elongation, and Nek10 is not known to be a stress‑induced outlier that would escape this effect.  Therefore the knockout is expected to decrease Nek10 mRNA levels.
